content: Freckles are clusters of concentrated melanin, which are most commonly observed in individuals with fair complexions. A freckle is also referred to as an ephelis. The presence of freckles is determined genetically and is associated with a variant of the melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) gene, which is a dominant trait. Freckles are frequently found in individuals with fair hair, such as blonde, strawberry blonde, dishwater blonde, or most commonly, red hair. The development of freckles is triggered by exposure to sunlight. Specifically, ultraviolet B (UV-B) radiation activates melanocytes, which then increase melanin production. This process causes freckles to darken and become more numerous. Freckles are predominantly located on the face but can appear on any area of the skin that is exposed to the sun. Freckles are rare in infants but are more commonly seen in children before puberty. They tend to be less common in adults. If freckles have been altered using creams or laser treatments and are not protected from sunlight, they will reappear upon sun exposure. However, in some cases, freckles may fade with age. Freckles are not considered a skin disorder. Individuals with freckles typically have a lower concentration of photoprotective melanin, making them more vulnerable to the harmful effects of UV radiation. It is important to avoid overexposure to UV radiation. Due to ongoing debates about the safety of sunscreen, protective clothing is recommended as the preferred method of sun protection. There are two types of freckles. The first type, known as ephelides, is a genetic trait. These freckles are flat, light brown or red in color, and tend to fade during the winter months. Ephelides are more common in individuals with light complexions and can be suppressed with the regular use of sunblock. The second type of freckle is referred to as liver spots, also known as sun spots or lentigines. Unlike ephelides, lentigines do not fade during the winter. Instead, they form after years of cumulative sun exposure and are more commonly observed in older individuals.
